content: Adverse reactions associated with cefadroxil include the following: 1. Gastrointestinal Reactions: Symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis may manifest during or after antibiotic treatment. Dyspepsia, nausea, and vomiting have been reported infrequently. Diarrhea has also been observed. 2. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Allergic reactions such as rash, urticaria, angioedema, and pruritus have been documented. These reactions typically resolve upon discontinuation of the drug. Anaphylaxis has also been reported. 3. Other Reactions: Cases of hepatic dysfunction, including cholestasis and elevations in serum transaminase levels, have been noted. Genital pruritus, genital moniliasis, vaginitis, moderate transient neutropenia, and fever have also been reported. Rarely, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, idiosyncratic hepatic failure, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, serum sickness, and arthralgia have been observed. 4. Additional Adverse Reactions and Laboratory Abnormalities: For cephalosporin-class antibiotics, additional adverse reactions have been reported, including toxic epidermal necrolysis, abdominal pain, superinfection, renal dysfunction, toxic nephropathy, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, hemorrhage, prolonged prothrombin time, positive Coombs’ test, increased blood urea nitrogen (BUN), increased creatinine, elevated alkaline phosphatase, elevated aspartate aminotransferase (AST), elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT), elevated bilirubin, elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), eosinophilia, pancytopenia, and neutropenia. 5. Seizures: Several cephalosporins, including cefadroxil, have been implicated in triggering seizures, particularly in patients with renal impairment when the dosage was not appropriately reduced. If seizures occur during drug therapy, the medication should be discontinued. Anticonvulsant therapy may be administered if clinically indicated.
